surface_mechanism_description: The reaction between WF6 and TiN/Ti barrier metals, described in eq. (2), may be suppressed when B2H6 is employed. It is known that the resistivity of a metal film is strongly affected by the grain size. This suggests that a W film on a B2H6-reduced nucleation layer may have larger grains than that on a SiH4-reduced nucleation layer.
evidence: The origin of the lower resistivity of the B2H6-reduced nucleation process was investigated. It may be explained by the following models. Model 1: It is known that CVD-W films contain a considerable amount of fluorine that may increase the resistivity of a W film. The authors have already reported that the B2H6-reduced nucleation film contains a lower concentration of fluorine than the SiH4-reduced film due to the higher reaction energy with WF6. This suggests that the fluorine concentration in the filling W layer is also decreased. Since the filling W layer has the largest thickness and the lowest resistivity in a W/TiN/Ti film stack, this decrease is expected to result in resistivity reduction. Model 2: The reaction between WF6 and TiN/Ti barrier metals, described in eq. (2), may be suppressed when B2H6 is employed. Model 3: It is known that the resistivity of a metal film is strongly affected by the grain size. This suggests that a W film on a B2H6-reduced nucleation layer may have larger grains than that on a SiH4-reduced nucleation layer. Model 4: The crystallization of the filling layer may be enhanced by the B2H6 nucleation process, although it has been reported that the B2H6-reduced film itself is amorphous.
